title: 146 skipIf silenciosos: a suite passa verde num host sem tmux em vez de falhar alto sobre dependencia ausente
description:
Medido em 2026-07-26: a suite tem 146 ocorrencias de .skipIf( distribuidas em 41 arquivos de teste, e zero ocorrencias de .skip(, .todo(, .only( ou .failing(. Na execucao completa neste host o relatorio junit registrou skipped igual a zero, ou seja todos os 146 predicados avaliaram falso porque tmux, git, bun e pgrep estao presentes na maquina. A consequencia e que num host que nao tenha alguma dessas dependencias, ate 146 testes simplesmente desaparecem da execucao e a suite reporta verde, sem nenhum sinal de que a verificacao foi parcial. Verde com buraco e indistinguivel de verde real.

Por que isso e risco e nao detalhe: o projeto ja tem cicatriz registrada dessa exata classe. O CAM-66 tratou skipIf como gate-gaming e o CAM-202 canonizou a doutrina de que gate vermelho e hard-stop e que dispensar falha como flaky, pre-existente ou ambiental e evasao proibida. Um skipIf que evapora silenciosamente e a versao estrutural do mesmo problema: em vez de um agente dispensar uma falha, a propria suite dispensa a verificacao. O CAM-186 ja mediu divergencia entre ambientes (in-container 2957 pass e 10 fail contra 3012 verdes no host), evidencia de que ambientes diferentes exercitam conjuntos diferentes de teste.

Por que agora: o repositorio e publico e o launch e o proximo marco. Um estranho que clone e rode a suite sem tmux instalado vai ver verde e concluir que verificou o produto. Para um produto cuja tese central de diferenciacao e verificacao falsificavel, uma suite que mente sobre o proprio escopo de verificacao e contradicao direta com a proposta de valor, alem de armadilha para qualquer contribuidor externo.

Direcao proposta, a validar na spec: tornar dependencia ausente um erro alto e nao um skip silencioso. Opcoes a avaliar na spec, sem escolher antecipadamente: (a) um preflight unico no inicio da suite que detecta as dependencias exigidas (tmux, git, pgrep) e falha imediatamente com mensagem acionavel listando o que falta, em vez de deixar cada arquivo decidir por conta; (b) manter o skip apenas sob um opt-in explicito e visivel, por exemplo uma variavel de ambiente deliberada, de modo que pular seja um ato consciente do operador e apareca no output; (c) fazer a contagem de testes pulados ser reportada e ratchetada, de modo que qualquer aumento de skips quebre o gate. Em todos os casos o requisito de aceitacao e o mesmo: em um host sem tmux a suite NAO pode terminar verde.

Requisitos de nao-regressao: a mudanca nao pode transformar em falha os casos legitimos onde o skip existe por razao ambiental valida e documentada; cada um dos 41 arquivos precisa ser triado para distinguir dependencia dura (ausencia deve falhar) de variacao ambiental legitima (ausencia pode pular, mas visivelmente e contabilizada). Registrar na issue a contagem final por categoria como evidencia.

Nota: esta issue nao economiza tempo de execucao e nao deve ser justificada por custo. O ganho e exclusivamente de robustez e honestidade do gate, alinhado ao ADR-0039 (o tier real-I/O existe justamente para impedir que fakes mintam) e a postura registrada em docs/agent-readiness.md de ranquear por merito de engenharia e nunca por custo operacional.

spec.scope:
Close the fully-silent verification hole in the test suite. Today `bun test` on a host without tmux drops 37 tests and still exits 0, which is indistinguishable from a real green. Deliver four things: (1) a single centralized dependency-probe helper, (2) a suite-level preflight that fails loud and actionably when a hard dependency is missing, unless the lane explicitly declares a waiver, (3) a per-lane skip-count ratchet so any future silent skip breaks the gate, and (4) deletion of the gating sites the preflight renders dead. Two lanes must both stay honest: the HOST lane (dev machines and the macos-latest `ci` job) has every dependency, permits no waiver, and must go RED when one is missing; the CONTAINER lane (.devcontainer and the `ci-container` job, which has no tmux by design) may stay green only under a named, counted waiver.

RE-SPEC NOTE. A first plan attempt escalated after two audit rounds with 3 criticals. The PRD architecture (helper + fail-loud preflight + waiver + ratchet) was judged sound and traceable to every issue AC; the auditor blocked exclusively on ORACLE defects that originated in this spec, not in the planner. The v1 spec expressed the centralization criteria as greps by BINARY NAME, which also match the legitimate real-I/O calls that ADR-0039 exists to protect: measured, that grep returns 132 lines on main of which only ~45 are probes, so it could never go green without deleting real test I/O. A second oracle (`grep -q 'ps' <file>`) was tautologically green on main, matching substrings like 'steps' and 'props'. Both defects share the recurring shape of the last three cycles (CAM-398 ordering, CAM-425 session-id, CAM-420 oracle): an assertion about the environment the claim is checked in, reasoned about instead of measured. Every oracle below has now been SWEPT against unmodified main at 44accd73 and its real output is recorded inline. Do not alter an oracle without re-sweeping it.

MEASURED CENSUS at 44accd73 (these numbers supersede both the issue text and the v1 spec, several of which were off by one or two):
- non-fixture `.skipIf(`: 146 lines / 41 files (repo-wide raw count is 153; 7 live in test/fixtures/version-skip-guard/ and are the guard's own fixtures)
- `skipIf(!gitAvailable`: 72 lines / 25 files
- `skipIf(!tmuxAvailable`: 42 lines / 13 files
- `skipIf(!jqAvailable`: 31 lines / 2 files
- probe DEFINITION sites: 45, spread over 41 files, with no helper module anywhere; var-name histogram gitAvailable 25, tmuxAvailable 14, jqAvailable 2, pgrepAvailable 2, bunAvailable 1, psAvailable 1, uuidgenAvailable 1
- files containing the token `tmuxAvailable`: 16 = 13 real probe files + 2 DI-fake option names (test/run.test.ts:82, test/stop.test.ts:58) + 1 guard fixture

MUST-SURVIVE INVENTORY (real wire-boundary I/O, protected by docs/adr/0039-cam-testing-philosophy-behavioral-di-fakes-plus-real-i-o-at-wire-boundaries-not-no-mocks-ever.md; deleting any of these to satisfy an oracle is a failed story, not a passing one): 73 real `spawnSync('git', ...)` non-version calls across 29 files; 18 real tmux driver calls of the form `spawnSync(tmux, ['-L', ...])` across 13 files (13 node-form + 5 Bun.spawnSync-form); 5 real `pgrep -f` calls in test/integration/orch-recycle-watch.test.ts; 1 real `ps -ax` call at test/integration/orch-recycle-pid-resolve.test.ts:89.

WHY THE ISSUE TEXT UNDERSTATES AND OVERSTATES. Understates: it never names the central design constraint, that the container lane has no tmux by design (the Dockerfile installs git and jq, zero tmux) and scripts/test-in-container.ts:12 documents verbatim that a run with only skips exits 0, so a blunt fail-loud breaks that lane; the waiver exists to resolve exactly that. Overstates: only the tmux drop is a false green. Dropping git or jq yields 37-38 HARD FAILURES alongside the skips, because many equally git-dependent tests are ungated, so those predicates protect nothing and merely advertise a git-less mode that does not work.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1 (centralization, primary oracle, swept): `grep -rnE "(const|let) [A-Za-z_]*[Aa]vailable *=" test --include='*.ts' | grep -vE 'test/helpers/|test/fixtures/'` returns EMPTY. Swept on unmodified main: 45 matching lines across 41 files, ZERO false positives (every one of the 45 is a probe declaration). This pattern is deliberately shaped on the DECLARATION form, not on binary names, and it provably does not touch the must-survive inventory. It also correctly ignores the two DI-fake sites: test/run.test.ts:82 is a `const { tmuxAvailable = true, ... } = opts` destructure (the `const {` blocks the regex) and test/stop.test.ts:58 is a property access (`handlers.tmuxAvailable === false`). Neither may be migrated or renamed.

AC2 (centralization, completeness oracle for the intermediate consts, swept): `grep -rnE "spawnSync\(\[?[\"'](tmux|git|jq|pgrep|ps|uuidgen|bun)[\"'](, *\[)?[^)]{0,60}(-V|--version)" test --include='*.ts' | grep -vE 'test/helpers/|test/fixtures/'` returns EMPTY. Swept on unmodified main: 39 matching lines, ZERO false positives once the fixture filter is applied (without that filter it also matches test/fixtures/version-skip-guard/legal-capability-skip.ts:6, which MUST survive). AC1 alone is insufficient: it misses two intermediate probe consts that are not named `*Available`, at test/integration/orch-recycle-pid-resolve.test.ts:41 (`const pgrepCheck = spawnSync('pgrep', ['--version'], ...)`) and :44 (`const bunCheck = spawnSync('bun', ['--version'], ...)`). AC1 and AC2 together are complete. Do NOT add an array-form binary-name pattern such as `Bun\.spawnSync\(\["tmux"`: swept, it returns 6 lines of which 5 are legitimate tmux driver calls in test/integration/sendkeys-submit.test.ts (:30, :34, :36, :49, :67) that must survive.

AC3 (fail loud, the defining oracle, swept): with every dependency present EXCEPT tmux, the suite must exit NON-ZERO with a message naming the missing binary and how to install it. Derive the environment, never hardcode it: `BUNBIN=$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$(command -v bun)")")` then `env -i HOME="$HOME" TERM="$TERM" PATH="$BUNBIN:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin" bun test; echo exit=$?`. That PATH still carries git, jq, pgrep, ps and uuidgen (all under /usr/bin or /bin) and omits only tmux. Swept on unmodified main: `5597 pass / 37 skip / 0 fail`, exit=0. Required after the fix: exit non-zero. An exit 0 under this exact command is a FAILED criterion no matter how many tests passed.

AC4 (control, no silent shrinkage, swept): full-PATH `bun test` reports `0 fail`, no skip line, exit 0, AND a parsed pass count of at least 5634 (the swept baseline at 44accd73: ` 5634 pass` / ` 0 fail`, exit 0, 78.84s). The pass-count floor is mandatory, not decorative: US-level deletion of gating sites makes it easy to delete a gated test BODY along with its predicate, which would still yield exit 0 with no skips, i.e. a smaller suite reported as a clean control. Record the floor in the same versioned lane file the ratchet uses so it is updated deliberately. Also run the PATH-surgery inertness control, the same `env -i` line as AC3 but WITH the tmux directory prepended, derived via `command -v tmux` + `readlink -f` + `dirname`: it must match the full-PATH result exactly (swept on main: identical, 5634 pass / 0 fail / 0 skip), proving any AC3 divergence is caused by this change and not by the surgery.

AC5 (container lane under a NAMED, COUNTED waiver): the container lane declares its missing dependency through an explicit, visible opt-in (env var or config key), never through silent predicate evaluation. With the waiver set, the tmux-gated tests skip and the run exits 0 AND the observed skip count EQUALS the count the waiver declares. With the waiver NOT set inside the container, the run exits non-zero. Do not accept a `grep -qi 'skip' <log>` style oracle: the existing harness already prints a skip count, so that grep is green today regardless of whether the waiver was wired, and only the exit-code half would carry signal. Assert the exact number. This replaces the policy written verbatim at scripts/test-in-container.ts:12 (`// A run with only skips (fail count 0) exits 0.`) and :150.

AC6 (ratchet, demonstrated red, not reasoned): the expected skip count for each lane is recorded in a versioned file and asserted by the gate; any run whose skip count differs from its lane's expectation fails with a message naming the delta. The demonstration must be EXECUTED: temporarily add one `test.skipIf(true)` case in a scratch test file, run the gate, observe FAILURE naming the +1 delta, then remove the scratch file and observe the gate pass. Report both observations verbatim in the handoff. Do not commit the scratch test. Parser constraint, swept: `bun test` OMITS the ` N skip` line entirely when the count is zero (a full-PATH run emits only ` 5634 pass`, ` 0 fail`, ` 12612 expect() calls`), so the parser must treat a missing line as zero, not as a parse failure, or the host lane breaks immediately.

AC7 (waiver semantics proven at the seam, replacing a tautological oracle): the v1 spec asserted the `ps` waiver with `grep -q 'ps' test/integration/orch-recycle-pid-resolve.test.ts`, which is green on unmodified main (the bare substring matches ~20 lines including 'steps' and 'props') and asserts nothing. Replace it with behavioral tests at the helper/preflight seam: injecting an absent hard dependency with NO waiver makes the preflight fail with a message naming that binary; injecting the same absence WITH the waiver declared makes the gated tests skip and the run exit 0. A DI-injected absence is required here and is ADR-0039-compliant, because the real-I/O route is unavailable: swept, `bun test test/integration/orch-recycle-pid-resolve.test.ts` under the AC3 tmux-less env exits 0 with `1 pass / 0 fail`, since that file's probes are pgrep/bun/ps, all of which live in /bin and /usr/bin and cannot be removed without creating symlinks. tmux remains the one genuinely separable binary and AC3 is the real-I/O proof for the mechanism as a whole.

AC8 (delete the dead gating sites): the 72 `skipIf(!gitAvailable` lines (25 files) and 31 `skipIf(!jqAvailable` lines (2 files) are DELETED, converting each gated test back to an ungated one. Justification is measured, not stylistic: git and jq exist in every lane we support (git, jq, pgrep, ps and uuidgen are preinstalled on the macos-latest runner image, and .devcontainer/Dockerfile installs git and jq), and their gating is already incoherent, since dropping git from PATH yields 37-38 hard failures from ungated but equally git-dependent tests. Deleting a gate must NOT delete the test body: this is the exact failure mode AC4's pass-count floor exists to catch. Oracle: `grep -rn "skipIf(!gitAvailable\|skipIf(!jqAvailable" test --include='*.ts'` returns empty (baseline 103 lines), with the AC4 floor holding.

AC9 (triage evidence): each of the 41 probe-bearing files is classified as hard-dependency or legitimate-environmental, and the final per-category counts are recorded in the handoff and PR body. The one site carrying a written rationale today is test/integration/orch-recycle-pid-resolve.test.ts:49-52 (`ps` is absent in oven/bun:1.2-slim, and the production recycle-watcher runs on the host, not in the container); it must remain skippable under a declared waiver rather than becoming a hard failure.

AC10 (doctrine coherence): scripts/check-version-skips.ts:15-18 currently records, as deliberate policy, that capability-probe skips `remain legal` and are not flagged, which is precisely why no existing gate can catch these 146 sites. After this change that comment is false by omission and must be updated to name the preflight and ratchet as the mechanism that now governs capability probes. Oracle: the file no longer asserts capability-probe skips are ungoverned, and `bun run check:all` is green.

AC11 (full quality spine per story, not just typecheck+test): every story that adds or rewrites TypeScript, a bunfig, a gate manifest entry or a CI workflow must run `bun run check:all` as an acceptance gate, per ADR-0023 and scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md. This is load-bearing here because the ratchet touches the GATES manifest, whose coherence is enforced by test/gates-manifest.test.ts and check:ci-parity INSIDE check:all, so a story stopping at `bun run typecheck` + `bun test` would miss its own regression. Swept baseline on main: `bun run check:all` exits 0 in 2:42.

AC12 (CI wiring traced, not assumed): .github/workflows/ci.yml installs tmux with `brew install tmux` before `bun run check:all`, and today nothing verifies that step worked; if it silently no-ops, CI stays green with a 37-test hole. After the fix a tmux-less host lane must go red. State in the handoff which lane the workflow selects and confirm the host lane sets NO waiver. Note that the `ci-container` job's heavy steps run only `if: steps.changes.outputs.container_changed == 'true'`, so the container lane is normally a neutral pass and a green PR is NOT evidence the waiver path works; prove that locally via the in-container harness.
domainTerms: lane: a distinct execution environment for the suite, with its own dependency set and its own declared waiver. Two exist today, the host lane (dev machines and the macos-latest `ci` job; all dependencies present; no waiver permitted) and the container lane (.devcontainer and the `ci-container` job; tmux absent by design).

waiver: an explicit, named, visible declaration that a lane lacks a hard dependency, replacing silent predicate evaluation. A waiver permits a specific set of tests to skip AND is counted, so the skipped set is asserted rather than merely tolerated.
ratchet: a versioned per-lane expected skip count (and pass-count floor) asserted by the gate. Any deviation fails, so a newly introduced silent skip cannot enter the suite unnoticed.
false green: a suite run that exits 0 while a set of tests silently did not execute. Measured today at exactly 37 tests on an otherwise-complete host that lacks tmux.

capability probe: an inline `spawnSync(bin, ['--version'|'-V'])` or `Bun.which(bin)` check whose boolean gates `test.skipIf`. All 45 probe declaration sites in scope are capability probes, and scripts/check-version-skips.ts whitelists them by name.

must-survive inventory: the real wire-boundary invocations of git, tmux, pgrep and ps inside test BODIES (73 + 18 + 5 + 1). They are protected by ADR-0039 and are the reason every centralization oracle here is shaped on the probe declaration form rather than on binary names.
gotchas: EVERY ORACLE IN THIS SPEC WAS SWEPT AGAINST UNMODIFIED MAIN AT 44accd73 AND ITS REAL OUTPUT IS RECORDED IN THE CRITERION. Do not invent, generalize or 'tighten' an oracle without re-sweeping it and restating the measured baseline. The v1 spec was blocked for exactly this: two oracles were reasoned about rather than measured, and neither could ever go green. patterns.md:899 bans this class.

THE BINARY-NAME TRAP, this is what escalated round 1: any grep matching a binary NAME (`spawnSync\('git'`, `spawnSync\('tmux'`, etc.) also matches the must-survive inventory. Measured, such a grep returns 132 lines on main of which only ~45 are probes; the other ~87 are real `git init`/`git add`/`git -C`, real `tmux -L <sock>` driver calls, real `pgrep -f` and a real `ps -ax`. Satisfying it would require deleting real test I/O, contradicting ADR-0039 and the curated test-quality invariant. Shape oracles on the DECLARATION form (AC1) plus the version-flag probe form (AC2).

Do NOT modify anything under test/fixtures/version-skip-guard/** (7 files, 7 `.skipIf` occurrences, including the only `isWindows` and `!process.env['CI']` predicates in the tree, plus legal-capability-skip.ts:6 which AC2's pattern would otherwise match). They are the fixtures for scripts/check-version-skips.ts and editing them breaks that gate. Both AC1 and AC2 carry the `grep -vE 'test/helpers/|test/fixtures/'` filter for this reason; removing the filter silently makes the oracle unsatisfiable.

THE ENVIRONMENT TRAP: derive every path, never hardcode. The Homebrew Cellar paths measured today (/opt/homebrew/Cellar/tmux/3.6a/bin, /opt/homebrew/Cellar/bun/1.3.13/bin) are version-pinned and drift on any brew upgrade. Use `command -v` + `readlink -f` + `dirname`. A hardcoded path turns AC3 into a tautology the moment either tool is upgraded.

tmux is the ONLY separable binary. git, jq, pgrep, ps and uuidgen all live in /usr/bin or /bin and cannot be dropped individually without creating symlinks, and creating symlinks to simulate is forbidden here because it fakes the very environment the oracle measures. tmux is separable only because Homebrew keeps it in its own Cellar directory. Consequence, measured: test/integration/orch-recycle-pid-resolve.test.ts is UNAFFECTED by the AC3 tmux-less env (it exits 0 with 1 pass there), so its waiver behavior must be proven at the DI seam per AC7, not by PATH surgery.

Do NOT write a criterion asserting that dropping git or jq currently produces a false green. It does not: it produces a red for the wrong reason (an unactionable pile of 37-38 hard failures instead of a named missing dependency). That distinction IS the defect for those sites and is why AC8 deletes rather than converts them.

The two DI-fake sites test/run.test.ts:82 and test/stop.test.ts:58 use the token `tmuxAvailable` as a fake option name, not as a probe. `grep -rln 'tmuxAvailable' test/` yields 16 files but only 13 are probe files. Migrating or renaming those two is out of scope and would break unrelated tests.

42 tmux `skipIf` sites map to only 37 skipped tests, because some files declare the predicate more times than they gate distinct test cases. Never treat site count and test count as interchangeable in an assertion; the ratchet counts TESTS, the centralization oracles count SITES.
`bun test` omits the ` N skip` summary line entirely at zero. Any ratchet or control parsing stdout must treat the missing line as zero.

tmux is already declared a hard runtime dependency at scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md:36 (`tmux (every session is a tmux split)`). The preflight message must enforce the documented policy, not invent a new one.

docs/adr/0039-cam-testing-philosophy-behavioral-di-fakes-plus-real-i-o-at-wire-boundaries-not-no-mocks-ever.md is load-bearing for this PRD and belongs in relatedDocs alongside docs/agent-readiness.md: it is the constraint that keeps the must-survive inventory out of the centralization sweep, and the justification for AC7's DI-injected absence.
